authoredSolutions.1: Surface tension has dimensions \([S] = MT^{-2}\), so \([S^{3/2}] = M^{3/2}T^{-3}\). Also \([\rho r^{3}] = (ML^{-3})(L^{3}) = M\). So the quoted formula is NOT dimensionally correct and the assertion is false, while the reason (dimensional analysis gives an R.H.S. of different dimension) is true. The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.2: With maximum height \(h\), the launch speed is \(u = \sqrt{2gh}\). Taking upward positive, the times at which the height is \(h/3\) satisfy \[\frac{h}{3} = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^{2} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{g}{2}t^{2} - \sqrt{2gh}\,t + \frac{h}{3} = 0.\] The two roots are \[t = \frac{\sqrt{2gh} \pm \sqrt{2gh - \frac{2gh}{3}}}{g} = \frac{\sqrt{2gh} \pm \sqrt{\frac{4gh}{3}}}{g}.\] The smaller root is the upward crossing and the larger the downward one, so \[\frac{t_{\text{up}}}{t_{\text{down}}} = \frac{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{4/3}}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{4/3}} = \frac{\sqrt{6} - 2}{\sqrt{6} + 2} = \frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}.\] The correct choice is B.
